standard_prerequisites.name: Definitions of entailment, joint satisfaction, unsatisfiability
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Opening of the same section: Gamma entails A iff every structure satisfying all of Gamma satisfies A; a set is unsatisfiable with no model
standard_prerequisites.use: Both directions are pure unfoldings of these clauses; negated-satisfaction is read as failure of satisfaction.

core_obligations: Forward (proof lines around 2262-2268): suppose Gamma entails A and some M satisfies Gamma + {not A}; then M satisfies A by entailment and fails A by the negation, contradiction - so no such M exists.
Reverse (lines 2269-2274): suppose the extension unsatisfiable; every M either misses Gamma or satisfies A; restricting to models of Gamma forces A, i.e. entailment.
proof_roadmap: Assume a counter-model to the entailment's negated extension.
Derive a satisfaction conflict at one structure.
Read the contrapositive back as entailment.
difficulty_reason: Semantic counterpart of the syntactic prov-incons law, proved directly (statement 2256-2260, proof 2261-2275): both directions fully written as quantifier chases over structures, nothing delegated; the three follow-up equivalences below it are posed as probs, outside the span. H2: complete two-directional semantic argument.
